questions.q: Temperature measured at weather stations is an example of...
questions.why: The phenomenon is continuous, but it is only measured at discrete locations. Interpolation estimates the values in between.

questions.q: Spatial interpolation rests on which assumption?
options: Spatial autocorrelation: nearby locations are more similar than distant ones
The process is stationary in time
questions.why: Because nearby points are related, you can use them to estimate the value at an unsampled location.

options: it always gives the right answer
the predictions depend entirely on the sample points and the weighting scheme, with no model of uncertainty
it can only be run once
questions.why: IDW doesn't model randomness, so it gives no uncertainty estimate.

questions.q: Raising the inverse distance power from 1 to 3 makes the surface...
options: more locally sensitive, because influence drops off quickly with distance
questions.why: With a higher p, nearby points dominate. With p = 1, distant points still contribute and the surface is smoother.

questions.q: How should you choose the pixel size of an IDW surface?
options: Based on the scale of the phenomenon and how dense the input points are
questions.why: Fine pixels suit dense data with lots of local variation. Coarse pixels suit sparse data or broad patterns.

questions.q: In a Gaussian random field, the observed values are treated as...
options: one realization of a random process, observed at discrete locations on a continuous surface
questions.why: The true surface exists everywhere, but we see only one realization of it at our sample points.

questions.q: On a semivariogram, the distance where the curve flattens out is the...
questions.why: Beyond the range, observations are effectively independent of each other.

questions.q: The nugget on a semivariogram represents...
options: the overall variance in the data
measurement error or very small-scale variation
the distance where points become independent
questions.why: The nugget is where the curve starts at zero distance. The sill is the plateau, which reflects overall variance.

questions.q: How does kriging choose its weights differently from IDW?
options: It uses a fitted variogram model, including how each sample point relates to every other one
questions.why: IDW weights by distance alone. Kriging's weights come from the modeled spatial dependence.

questions.q: Where is the kriging variance (uncertainty) highest?
options: Right next to a sample point
In areas with sparse or distant observations
Only at the edges of the map
questions.why: Dense, strongly correlated nearby points give low uncertainty. Gaps between stations give high uncertainty.

questions.q: Which of these does kriging give you that IDW does not?
options: An estimate of uncertainty at each location
questions.why: Both produce weighted-average surfaces. Only the probabilistic method also estimates how uncertain each prediction is.

questions.q: Adding elevation as a covariate to a temperature interpolation lets the model...
options: use both spatial structure and an external variable that drives the values
questions.why: Covariates move beyond proximity alone by bringing in factors that shape the surface, such as elevation, land cover or soil.
